response: Nontriploid partial hydatidiform moles do not exist. These types of moles are thought to be less likely to occur due to the genetic changes that typically characterize triploid partial hydatidiform moles, which often involve multiple sets of chromosomes (triploidy). The fact that putative specimens in some studies show pathologic or ploid errors suggests that nontriploid partial moles may indeed exist. However, careful reevaluation of these specimens will likely uncover such errors in most cases.
